newsitem.title: CANADA: BCE falls on Bell's lower profit outlook.
newsitem.headline: BCE falls on Bell's lower profit outlook.

text.p: Shares of BCE Inc fell in second most active trading in Toronto on Thursday after its Bell Canada unit lowered its forecast for 1997 profits.
BCE fell as much as 3.30 to 65.90 in early trading before recovering partly to 67.40, down 1.80 from Wednesday's close, on about 2.2 million shares.

Analysts said BCE stock was down mainly because of an announcement by Bell Canada late on Wednesday in which the telephone company lowered its 1997 profit outlook to C$850 million from C$950 million forecast previously.
"It's that, and the stock may have been getting expensive," said an analyst who declined to be identified.

BCE shares have rallied over the past several weeks, mainly on its strong year-end earnings, declining cost structure and strengthening balance sheet. BCE is Canada's most widely held stock and has strong retail and instututional investor followings. Bell Canada is the country's biggest phone company.
Analyst John Drolet, of Yorkton Securities, said he is lowering his 1997 profit outlook for BCE to about C$3.60 a share from C$4, based mainly on the lower profit outlook at Bell Canada.
In 1996, BCE posted a net profit of C$1.15 million or C$3.40 a share, after a one-time gain, net of provisions, of C$125 million or C$0.39 a share.

On Wednesday night, Bell Canada forecast net income available to common shares of C$850 million in 1997, up from C$714 million in 1996, but down from the C$950 million forecast in March 1995 in a filing with Canadian regulators.
Bell also said it anticipated operating cash flow of C$3 billion for 1997, up from C$2.8 billion in 1996, and free cash flow of C$150 million, down from C$204 million in 1996.
